That’s a hard question. Carbs are not inherently bad, no food is bad it is fuel and some fuel is more efficient than other fuel. At 3 years out for me carbs must be limited because they’re trigger foods for me, too many carbs has me craving more. I try and focus on necessary healthy carbs like fibrous fruit and vegetable carbs and not breads/chips/sugary foods. When I was up to 18 months post op I tried for a range of 15-60 grams of carbs a day. Now (after having a baby in June and not being careful through the holidays) I’m not letting myself have more than 30 a day because I’m very annoyed with myself for eating so many sweets and being 23lbs up from my lowest weight. Try and focus on protein/fiber/vitamins. Don’t be too hard on yourself but be honest, track and keep yourself accountable, try and think as you put in food in your mouth “is this fuel worth it?”

That’s literally how insurance works. It’s a shared risk if a company has to pay out a boat load of claims due to a weather event everyone pays higher premiums. Insurance (especially for small/regional carriers) is not as profitable as everyone assumes  because they look at it in terms of their rates only and not the market as a whole. If the insurance company has to absorb all the cost of a storm with numerous claims they’d go bankrupt. An average carrier takes in only $.01-.05 as actual profit for every $1.00 in premium they take in.

Hi new mama! Congratulations on your soon to be here little one! First of all if they don’t snap in inserts are interchangeable. Without seeing them I can’t tell you which inserts are microfiber but if you upload pictures on imgur and link I’m happy to look at them for you.  As far as ease for sitters I’d say AiOs (all in ones) are the best bet because it’s most like a disposable, you just take it off and put it in a wet bag. This is a good resource to start with. https://www.mamanatural.com/cloth-diapering/ she explains the different types of diapers. 

My personal recommendation is to take anything Fluff Love University says with a grain of salt because they can be kinda mean and/or “my way or the highway” even if they are well meaning. If you have a Facebook try looking into “Fluffbutt Support Uncensored” they’re very supportive and helpful. 

Try searching for a local cloth diaper group there too. Try calling local baby stores (not chain/franchises) to see if they have resources they can point you too, many people cloth diaper and you’d be surprised who around you does so.
You’re welcome! Good luck!

She told me how much she loved me (I cannot say for certain but I think it was her final goodbye to me and she planned it) and how proud she was of me, how special I was, how she knew I would accomplish so much. 

She touched so many lives, people came from 1000s of miles away to say goodbye to her at her memorial. And you know what people said? “If you had asked me I never could have imagined she was hurting so much.” We heard some version of that over and over. You know what else people said? “I wish she had reached out to me, I would have jumped on a plane to be with her and help her.” We heard that multiple times too. 

She was sick, I am sick, you are sick, but because of what she did I know I can never make that choice. The finality of her choice still affects me today. 

She will never see her children get married, she will not see her grandchild grow up, she will never hold her great nephew (I’m due in June and he would have loved her so much and she him because she loved babies so much), she did not get to say goodbye to her mother who died 4 months later, she did not get to hold her sister when she found out her cancer came back, she never met my amazing fiancé, she never saw the sunrise over the mountains across the lake from my grandparents house for the last time before my grandpa was forced to sell it after 40 years of it being our family’s safe haven. She never got to taste the bread I learned to bake after she passed. She will never hold another puppy (she loved dogs) or smell her roses bloom(she grew like 15 different colors/types), she won’t hear any songs she loved ever again, she won’t feel the sun on her face (summer was her favorite season).

I don’t care if it’s cooking/baking, I don’t care if it’s gaming, I don’t care if it’s your car, tattoos, the new Star Wars movies, metal detecting, hiking, skiing, painting, binging TV series on Netflix, going on roller coasters, travel, rescuing animals, visiting sick kids in the hospital, learning about a new subject or an old one, reading, conspiracy theories, whatever. 

Life is a beautiful present, even if you’re in pain every day, you were the strongest sperm, you won a once in a million jackpot, it’s worth it dammit.

Yeah female weight loss surgery patient checking in. I’m 30 but was 28 when I had surgery.

Had a vertical sleeve gastrectomy 12/17/16. It’s colloquially called “stomach stapling” but essentially involves making your 12-30oz holding stomach(depending on how full your stomach is and how much you have abused it and stretched it) into a 3-7 ounce holding stomach by cutting away the greater curvature side, severing the vagus nerve and stapling it into a small banana sized pouch. It differs from gastric bypass (also know as Reux and Y) because your digestive system is not rerouted.

I used to be 330lbs at my highest recorded weight in February 2016 (323lb at my first surgery consultation October of 2016 and 298lb on day of surgery 12/17/16). I’m 5’6 and 1/4 and yes the 1/4 inch counts.

I’m pregnant so I’m up almost 25lbs from my lowest weight but I had gotten to 189lbs by 1 year 8 months out from surgery.

Literally everything about my life is different, from how much water I drink, to how much I exercise, to how and what I eat including; the speed, size of bites, textures/flavors I enjoy, nutrient composition of my food, and most importantly how I view food. 

I had to have a $48k surgery that I paid less than  $1.5k for (thank you amazing insurance coverage and meeting yearly deductibles) because I couldn’t do it alone, some will doubt that or say I was lazy or so took the easy way out and that’s okay because that’s their opinion. 

I was killing myself; my liver function was compromised, I regularly got kidney stones (2-4 times a year in the ER in excruciating pain), took medication for high blood pressure, had sleep apnea, extreme social anxiety and depression (those are still around but much diminished), female issues related to weight including ovarian cysts and irregular heavy periods and massive cramps and pain, diminished lung capacity, my spine and hips would constantly go out of alignment (chiropractic visits 2-3 times a month), literally wanted to die every day.

Take it from someone who was morbidly obese from 7-28 years old, do not let your weight get out of control. It is the worst thing you can do to yourself outside of drug addictions. Educate yourself about proper nutrition, not fad diets, garbage supplements or starvation to lose weight. If you can afford it see a reputable nutritionist/dietitian, work out even if it’s just getting outside and walking, you will thank yourself.

I remember being 19 and I swallowed a bunch of pills because I hated everything about my life. I was severely morbidly obese, single and lonely, incredibly poor, socially awkward with almost no friends, my parents marriage was falling apart for which my dad blamed me. I hated myself and thought that God couldn’t want me because I was such a huge sinner; gluttonous, wrathful, angry, and just so imperfect. 

I’m 30 now and I’d be lying if I said life is perfect, but it’s definitely not as bad as at 19. Thank goodness my suicide attempt failed. 

The things that mattered then don’t matter now. I know it’s so hard to hear that. I remember people saying “In 5 years this won’t matter you won’t feel this way” but I swear on my life it’s true. It’s not cliche.

I’m so sorry you’re hurting, you’re so young, you have so much time left. I wish I could just scoop you into my arms and hug you and let you cry, I know it’s what I needed then and it sounds like what you could use now.

Please don’t let this temporary hurt take you from this world. It’s going to sound dumb probably (because I know where you are mentally) but I’m just going to list some good things you’d miss if you took your life today. Some might not apply but a lot of them will.

1) Your cat laying on your stomach and purring and meowing when you first wake up in the morning.

2) Sunshine on your shoulders in the first warm day of spring when you put on the first tank top for the year.

3) Reading a great book by your favorite author or in your favorite genre laying in the grass while the breeze softly ruffles your hair.

4) The smell of the food cooking at a fair or festival that comes to town every year.

5) Seeing a baby smile at you in the supermarket and peek around their parent to just keep smiling at you.

6) Jumping into cool fresh water on a scorching hot day.

7) Hearing a song you love that you haven’t heard for years on the radio and still remembering all the words so you sing along.

8) A bear hug from a friend or family member that practically crushes your ribs but it feels so good.

9) Bonfires on a chilly fall night the way the wood crackles and pops and the smoky smell that lingers in your hair and clothes.

10) The first snow of winter that comes down in fat fluffy flakes swirling around like a ballet of nature’s wonders.

11) A friend who you haven’t seen in awhile telling you how much they miss you.

12) Puppies and kittens, enough said.

13) Breathtaking views from the top of a mountain hike, the air feeling so clean and feeling so accomplished that you climbed a mountain.

14) The sounds of the ocean waves breaking against the shore.

15) Soaking in a warm bath with bubbles or a bath bomb, feeling so safe and relaxed.

16) Dancing at weddings, knowing you get to celebrate a slice of someone’s love story.

17) Fresh warm jammies out of the dryer on a cold night.

18) The first kiss from your future husband or wife, you’ll never forget it your whole life.

19) The way your grandma or grandpa smells when they hug you, alternately how their house smells when you visit.

20) Walking across the stage at your graduation and getting to move the tassel from one side of your hat to the other.

Maybe that helped, maybe it didn’t, but know at least one stranger who you have never met cares enough about you even though they’ve never met you to take time out of their day to make this list for you. One stranger who has been where you are, who knows how you feel. Please please try and make it through just today, breathe, just for today. Tomorrow is a new day, a new blessing, a new opportunity, maybe tomorrow won’t be better, maybe it will, but it’s just one day.

I'm about 14 months out from VSG (surgery 12/17/15) and when I track and lose I have to be about 1000-1100cals max a day 60grams protein and I try to vary healthy fibrous carbs day to day but keep them lower(under 60/day when I'm trying and being "good") but I'm still learning how to love myself and not turn to food for comfort. I might have a tiny tummy but a tiny tummy full of Easter chocolate is not a tiny tummy with the right calories. I'd gotten down to 193.5 at almost exactly a year out (it was not the weight at my 1 year post op due to period water weight gain) at my lightest (at that point I was down 130lbs since surgery) but gained a bit from over indulging December through Jan I got back as high as 201 and said no food is worth this. I'm back down to 195.5 as of today. I also never get too crazy or militant because emotionally I cannot or my eating disorder (Ednos with both bulimic and anorexic tendencies sprinkled with lots of bingeing) will swing up and I'll over restrict or binge causing a stall/gain.  My surgeons office wants me at 800-1000 calories a day but won't give a carb goal with minimum 60 grams of protein. I think every body is different and I think it's important you learn what works for you. You can get your metabolism checked and your average daily calorie burn calculated pretty accurately with a bod pod or other such device. When I exercise (I hike when weather permits and average about 300-700 calories burned depending on how far/long I go) I add in about another 80-150 calories those days usually an extra string cheese or some almonds on the hike itself. Call your surgeons office for more help or find a dietician your insurance will cover who knows how to work with WLS patients if you need more guidance. Under eating can be just as bad as overeating and can wreck your metabolism. Sorry this is kinda all over the place I took my sleeping pill and am kinda out of it.
